statement: For the degree-three member with all eight point constraints real and generic, exactly the real counts 8,10,12 are attainable. Consequently the minimum is 8 and the maximum is 12.

answer.text: For the degree-three member with all eight point constraints real and generic, exactly the real counts 8,10,12 are attainable. Consequently the minimum is 8 and the maximum is 12.

source.location: Proposition 4.7.3 and preceding “Digression: real rational curves”, printed p.50

scope: Degree d=3 in the rational-plane-curve family, with eight generic real point constraints.
notes: The extracted result covers only d=3 and all-real constraints; it does not determine the minimum or maximum in every degree or for mixed conjugate data.
